discovery: Discovery of intrinsic long-range magnetic order in atomically thin van der Waals crystals

nominees.name: Xiang Zhang
nominees.affiliation: The University of Hong Kong, China

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D magnetism and quantum materials)
motivation: In 2017, Xu and Jarillo-Herrero (CrI3, monolayer Ising ferromagnetism and layer-dependent antiferromagnetism) and Zhang (Cr2Ge2Te6, few-layer Heisenberg ferromagnetism) showed that long-range magnetic order survives down to single atomic layers when magnetic anisotropy lifts the Mermin-Wagner restriction. This experimental result created the field of 2D magnets. Within a few years it gave giant tunneling magnetoresistance in spin-filter junctions, electrical and gate control of magnetism, and van der Waals heterostructures where magnetism couples to excitons, valleys and topology. It also opened new spectroscopic windows. Magneto-optical Kerr, Raman, second-harmonic and terahertz probes of atomically thin magnets now reveal magnons, magnetoelectric coupling and spin-entangled excitons in CrI3, CrSBr, NiI2 and related materials. These platforms have become a standard testbed for controlling quantum materials with fields and light.
